items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: That's the only time I ever played with punch was an advertisement.

ctx.x: I like world rules and I like high society too. Do you like a lot of marches? No. No. I like Timberlaine. I like Timberlaine too. It's good. Several others are. I like Barry, no. I just can't think of them now. I've been in Gettysburg, you like that? Yeah. What about punch? Did you ever play with punch much? I never played with punch. I believe the only time I played with punch was on an advertisement. You know, like they used to advertise on a Sunday evening for a dance, at night, for a couple of hours. That's…
I know Bill Russell told me that you wanted to record with Percy. What's that? Bill Russell had told me that you wanted to record with Percy. Way back.

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: Well I guess I only had the opportunity to play one job with him and that was an advertisement.

ctx.x: He had a big tone. He was pretty strong, he had a big tone. He played, he was a kid punch clarinet.
Oh that's right, yeah. Did you ever play with punch too or any time?
Well I guess I only had the opportunity to play one job with him and that was an advertisement. On the truck. On the truck. Yes.
